papers.title: Personalizing Dialogue Agents: I have a dog, do you have pets too?
papers.evidence: Original work evaluates persona-conditioned next-utterance prediction, including likelihood and candidate classification, and compares IR and profile-memory models. It separately uses human dialogue judgments and warns about trivial persona word overlap. Its personas are assigned fictional profiles, not authentic speaker identities.
papers.decision: Recognition is an established research endpoint, not an invented fidelity metric. Reciprocal real-speaker candidates and option-order controls are a bounded adaptation. No semantic appropriateness or generative fidelity follows from corpus-reference selection alone.

papers.title: Evaluating Dialogue Generation Systems via Response Selection
papers.read: Sections2-4 including false-candidate construction, human filtering and metric comparison
papers.evidence: Random alternatives can be unrelated or genuinely acceptable; their benchmark explicitly uses human filtering to support quality evaluation. Their reported system-ranking correlation does not license arbitrary automatic distractor labels as semantic truth.
papers.decision: PersonaSLM will report recognition of what actually occurred, not classify the reciprocal foil as semantically unacceptable. Current study does not replace pending Japanese human review or claim the paper validates its Japanese endpoint.
